what: Master Version 2.26 — Lionel MPC-Modern slipped descriptions put back on their own numbers: in 63 stretches the words (Item Type, Sub-Type, Control, Road Name, Description, Gauge, Year Produced) had slid one row (a few two) against the item numbers; each row now carries the words that match its own lionel.com Reference Link. About 60 rows whose own words were lost at the end of a stretch are rebuilt from Lionel's page name (years from the book where the book has the line). Also 37 steam locomotives typed Accessory (4-4-0 brass hybrids, Big Boys, S1s, 4-6-0s, Camelbacks, AC-12s, Generals) set to Steam Locomotive.
stated: Brad (2026-10-10): "i think we have another missed line or something"; "yes" to starting the slipped rows; "yes" to writing MPC_SLIPPED_ROWS_REVIEW_2026-10-10.xlsx as one edit

why: The Reference Link (column M) ends in each item's own Lionel number and names the product, so it is the answer key (same doctrine as the August 2026 repair). Book page photos show the item numbers printed about half a line off their descriptions, which is how the typed-in list paired numbers with the wrong line.
unchanged: Item numbers, Reference Links, Variation # / Variation Details, Notes, Est. Market Value, Source, COTT columns, Stamped Markings, Row IDs; every other row. Rows listed for later (no change now): descriptions whose number has no row, 7 extra repeated-number rows, 32 unlinked rows to check against the book photos, 27 rows left alone (Lionel and the book disagree). All in MPC_SLIPPED_ROWS_REVIEW_2026-10-10.xlsx.
toPutBack: Write each cell's old value back to its row (find by item number + Row ID).
